thesis: PepsiCo is the watchlist's defensive outlier: Q1 2026 beat on both lines (revenue $19.44B, core EPS $1.61, organic +2.6%) with North American food volumes back to growth, an Elliott Management settlement ($4B stake) driving a margin-and-focus turnaround plan, and a ~4% dividend yield at 22.5x earnings. The uncomfortable arithmetic underneath: last year the dividend consumed 105% of earnings and 111% of free cash flow, leverage sits at ~2.45x debt-to-equity, and GLP-1-era consumption shifts pressure the snacks core. Q2 2026 earnings land July 9 - tomorrow - with analysts cutting targets into the print.
catalysts: Q2 2026 earnings July 9, 2026 - analysts have trimmed targets; the $144 level is being watched
Elliott turnaround execution: margin expansion, portfolio focus (bottling-light strategy), accelerated organic growth
FY2026 guidance affirmed: organic +2-4%, core cc EPS +4-6%, $8.9B total cash returns
Any dividend-coverage improvement (FCF growth vs the $7.9B dividend)
risk_factors: Dividend coverage: payout was 105% of earnings and 111% of FCF last year - the 4% yield is borrowed, not earned, until FCF grows
GLP-1 and health-driven consumption shifts are a structural headwind to the salty-snack core
Leverage: debt-to-equity ~2.45 constrains flexibility if cash returns must be defended
Elliott-driven restructuring carries execution risk (plant changes, cost cuts, leadership turnover)
Low growth: organic +2.6% means the equity case depends almost entirely on margin expansion and the multiple

q1_2026_revenue.note: beat by ~500M; core EPS 1.61 vs 1.55 expected, +9% y/y; organic growth +2.6%

fy2026_guidance.note: core cc EPS +4-6%; cash returns ~8.9B (7.9B dividends + 1.0B buybacks)

dividend_payout_ratios.unit: ratio of earnings and FCF respectively
dividend_payout_ratios.note: prior-year payout exceeded both earnings and FCF

elliott_stake.note: settled with board agreement; turnaround plan in execution
